newsitem.title: KENYA: Aid workers find thousands of refugees in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Aid workers find thousands of refugees in Zaire.

text.p: Aid workers found thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees on Monday trekking south of the northeast Zairean city of Kisangani, the U.N. World Food Programme said.

"The team which went out today radioed back they have found thousands of refugees on the road between km 30 (mile 19) and km 41 (mile 25), heading southwards," said WFP spokeswoman Michele Quintaglie.
"They said they found thousands but gave no more details. This is very good news. We have a train fully loaded with 115 tonnes of food which we will dispatch to them tomorrow," she added.
Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila gave aid agencies 60 days from May 1 to repatriate all Rwandan Hutu refugees from Zaire after up to 100,000 last week fled into the jungle south of Kisangani.
Aid workers said it would be virtually impossible to meet the deadline. In addition to the 100,000 south of Kisangani, 250,000 Rwandan and 50,000 Burundian refugees are unaccounted for in Zaire.
